# Examples

Seven complete documents for `@inkoxide/render`, one file each. They style with `className`, so
install `@inkoxide/tailwind` next to `@inkoxide/render`. Every file exports its component and
sample data, and renders `<name>.pdf` when you run it:

```sh
npx tsx invoice.tsx
```

<!-- examples:start (generated by examples/render.ts) -->

| File | Shows |
|---|---|
| `receipt.tsx` | The README's quick start: an A6 receipt with a total. |
| `invoice.tsx` | An SVG logo, a table whose header repeats on every page, totals kept together and page numbers in the footer. |
| `report.tsx` | Three KPI cards, a bar chart drawn with SVG, a 60-row table across three pages, a header from page 2 on, and bookmarks. |
| `certificate.tsx` | A landscape page, nested borders, the Inter Display face, a drawn seal and an absolutely positioned serial number. |
| `letter.tsx` | US Letter, justified and hyphenated paragraphs, a mailto: link and a footer between the page margins. |
| `resume.tsx` | A CSS grid with a full-height sidebar, tags that wrap, and jobs that never split across pages. |
| `form.tsx` | Text fields, a select, radio buttons and checkboxes that can be filled in any PDF viewer. |

<!-- examples:end -->

`pnpm --filter @inkoxide/examples render` renders all of them to `out/`, writes the first page of
each to `packages/react/media/`, framed as a sheet of paper on a grey canvas, and rewrites the
quick start, gallery and examples sections of `packages/react/README.md` from these files, so the
README always shows the code that made each picture. It needs poppler (`pdftoppm`).
